([[Pankow (locality)|Berlin-Pankow, Germany]]) | college = [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2015–2018) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = 2014 | years1 = 2014–2015 | team1 = [[Alba Berlin]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] (2018) * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|Big Ten Tournament]] MVP ([[2018 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2018]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry| {{bk|GER}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|FIBA Europe U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B|2014 Bulgaria]] | [[Germany national under-19 basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Victor Moritz Wagner''', also known as '''Mo''', or '''Moe Wagner''' (born April 26, 1997) is a German basketball player. He played for [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|University of Michigan]] from 2015 through his junior season for the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 Wolverines team]]. Wagner stands 6’11’’ (211 cm) tall and plays the forward position. He entered his name for the [[2017 NBA draft]] without hiring an agent, but withdrew and returned to Michigan. He was a 2018 All-Big Ten second team selection by both the coaches and the media. Following the season, he was the [[2018 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament]] MVP helping the team earn the Big Ten Tournament championship for the second time in a row. He was also named to the West Region All-Tournament Team and Final Four All-Tournament Team during the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Basketball Tournament]]. He has represented the [[Germany national basketball team]] in international play and played professionally in the [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. ==Youth career== [[File:20170301 NW-UM Moe Wagner at the rim.jpg|Wagner in the paint for the [[2016–17 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2016–17 Michigan Wolverines]]|thumb|left]] Wagner started his basketball career in the youth ranks of [[Alba Berlin]]. In the 2011-12 season, he made his first appearance on the club’s under-16 Bundesliga team and emerged into a key player on the team the following season.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/teams/jbbl/nordost/#rcd1:/statistik/spieler/index.php%253Fteam_id=2014&pos=&spieler_id=23302&saison=2012|title=Teams der JBBL Nordost|website=NBBL und JBBL|language=de-DE|access-date=March 3, 2016}} In 2013-14, Wagner gained his first experiences at the senior level, playing for Berlin’s second team in the [[List of Regionalligen#Basketball|Regionalliga]], the fourth-tier of German basketball,{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketball-bund.net/statistik.do?reqCode=spielerstatistik&_top=-1&_absolut=0|title=BBL GmbH|website=www.basketball-bund.net|access-date=March 3, 2016}} while also competing for the club’s under-19 Bundesliga squad,{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/teams/nbbl/nordost/#rcd1:/statistik/spieler/index.php%253Fteam_id=1008&pos=&spieler_id=23302&saison=2014|title=Teams der NBBL Nordost|website=NBBL und JBBL|language=de-DE|access-date=March 3, 2016}} helping the team capture the German championship.{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketball-bund.de/news/top4-alba-berlin-kroent-nbbl-meister-139062|title=TOP4: ALBA Berlin krönt sich zum NBBL-Meister « Deutscher Basketball Bund|website=www.basketball-bund.de|access-date=March 3, 2016}} In 2014-15, he landed a spot on Berlin’s [[Basketball Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] roster and made his debut in the German top-flight on October 2, 2014, scoring six points in 6 minutes and 15 seconds of play against [[BG Göttingen]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.beko-bbl.de/de/statistiken/spieler/portraits/p/23302-moritz-wagner/|title=Beko BBL - 23302 Moritz WAGNER|website=www.beko-bbl.de|access-date=March 3, 2016}} He also saw (little) playing time in the [[2014–15 Euroleague|Euroleague]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=005758&seasoncode=E2014|title=WAGNER, MORITZ - Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL|website=www.euroleague.net|access-date=March 3, 2016}} ==College career== The first [[college basketball]] game that Wagner ever saw was the April 8, [[2013 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game]] in which [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] defeated the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 Wolverines]].{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2018/03/24/michigans-moritz-wagner-having-time-his-life-ncaa-tournament/455003002/|title=Michigan's Moritz Wagner having time of his life in NCAA tournament|accessdate=April 4, 2018|date=March 24, 2018|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}} He downloaded the game and watched it on an [[iPad]].{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/columnists/mitch-albom/2018/03/29/moritz-wagner-mitch-albom-michigan-basketball-john-beilein/468101002/ |title= How Moritz Wagner came to Michigan: An iPad, John Beilein and garlic |accessdate= April 4, 2018 |date= March 29, 2018 |author= Albom, Mitch |work= [[Detroit Free Press]]}} Wagner then saw the [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14 Wolverines]] lose in the elite eight round of the [[2014 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]] to [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] with his father, Axel. The hysteria of [[March Madness]] and college basketball caught his attention and interest. Wagner first came to the attention of [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|University of Michigan]] head coach [[John Beilein]] in 2014 through an email from a former coaching acquaintance in Germany. By one account, after watching a video of Wagner, Beilein called former Alba Berlin player [[Johannes Herber]], who Beilein had coached for four years at [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia University]] (WVU). In a 2018 interview, Herber recalled that during their conversation, he brought up the similarity between Wagner's playing style and that of one of Herber's former WVU teammates, noting "I knew from the way coach used [[Kevin Pittsnogle|Kevin [Pittsnogle]]] that Moe could be a good fit in that offense."{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22922995/ncaa-tournament-final-four-moe-wagner-michigan-wolverines-career-really-dream-come-true |title=Moe Wagner's Michigan career really is a dream come true |first=Joel |last=Anderson |website=ESPN.com |date=March 27, 2018 |accessdate=March 27, 2018}} By another account, Wagner used social contacts to forward a self-made highlight video to Beilein, which Beilein replied to. However, Beilein's reply sat in Wagner's spam folder for two weeks until Beilein made contact with Wagner by a personal visit to Germany. Shortly after Beilein's conversation with Herber, he began his recruitment of Wagner with phone calls. He recalled in 2018, "So I just said, you know what? We can't like sit on this. I think this kid is going to be pretty good, but nobody's been over to see him." Beilein followed through on this with a flight to Berlin to meet with Wagner and his family, in which he tried to convince them the advantages of American college basketball over a European professional contract. During the process, Wagner also reached out to Herber, with Herber recalling, "He was just curious. It's easy to fall in love watching college basketball on TV and want to be here. And the good thing about Moe is that he was very confident about his ability." ===Freshman season=== Wagner announced his decision to play at Michigan for the [[2015–16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2015–16 season]] in April 2015.{{Cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12623456/german-forward-moritz-wagner-commits-michigan-wolverines|title=Wolverines pick up German prospect Wagner|author=Borzello, Jeff|website=ESPN.com|date=April 5, 2015|access-date=March 3, 2016}} By opting to go to college, he turned down an offer to play professionally.{{Cite web|url=http://www.berliner-zeitung.de/sport/alba/alba-berlin--der-wechsel-von-albas-talent-moritz-wagner-ist-eine-systemfrage-1132042|title=Alba Berlin : Der Wechsel von Albas Talent Moritz Wagner ist eine Systemfrage {{!}} Berliner Zeitung|last=Schwager|first=Christian|website=Berliner Zeitung|language=de-DE|access-date=March 3, 2016}} On March 16 in the First Four round of the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]], Michigan defeated [[2015–16 Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball team|Tulsa]], 67–62.
